elements.element: Customer has no non-compete or field-of-use restriction.
elements.evidence: Revised 12.4 reads "Customer may develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory," removing the prohibition and the 24-month post-term tail; no other operative text binds Customer with a compete, field-of-use, or territory restriction, and 12.3 affirmatively confirms "Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete... commitment."

elements.element: The restriction covers only a named competing product.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no restriction on Customer survives after the edit, so there is nothing whose product scope needs narrowing; the preferred outcome exceeds this fallback constraint.

elements.element: The restriction applies during the term only.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the term-plus-24-months tail in original 12.4 was deleted and no restriction remains to have any temporal reach.

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: with the prohibition removed there is no duration to cap; the walk-away 24-month post-term restraint is gone.

elements.element: The restriction permits Customer's internal development.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: revised 12.4 expressly permits Customer to "develop... any product or service that competes with Vendor," and 12.3 confirms nothing restricts Customer from developing any product or service.
Condition does not apply: revised 12.4 expressly permits Customer to "acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory."

reasons: Preferred checklist is complete: the sole element is met in operative language, not merely promised in the margin comment — the prohibition, its 24-month post-term tail, and the "in any territory" field/territory reach are all eliminated from Section 12.4.

The edit is confined to the offending sentence in 12.4. It adds no survival tail, no expense allocation, no procedure, and no requirement outside the NONCOMPETE checklist, and it leaves Section 12.3 (favourable to Customer) untouched.

Reversing 12.4 into a permission rather than deleting the paragraph keeps the numbering intact and avoids dangling cross-references; note that the permission largely restates 12.3's existing "Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service... in any field or territory," so a straight deletion of 12.4 would be equally acceptable and marginally cleaner if the counterparty objects to the restatement.

Intent is preserved: the internal contradiction between original 12.4 and Vendor's acknowledgement in 12.3 that Customer gave no non-compete commitment is resolved, and no allocation, timing, remedy, or commercial mechanic elsewhere is disturbed.
Deterministic checks are consistent with the substance: no open-ended "competes with Vendor" prohibition binding Customer remains anywhere in the rendered text.

The "deviation" classification is correct on the original — a term-plus-24-month restraint over "any product or service that competes with Vendor" is walk-away on both duration and undefined scope, so it could not be left at the fallback.
